text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — gpu-node-17 (rack-b) reported kernel panic and kubelet went NotReady. Initial symptoms: oom-kill + watchdog reset. Alert ID: PD-83472.

pagerduty: Auto-page to eng-oncall @channel — please ack.

alex: Acked. I’m on it.

priya: What’s the customer impact? Any 5xxs or throttles showing up?

murtaza: I’m looking at prometheus and k8s metrics. Node lost heartbeat at ~1964567878. Affected pods: 12 pods (mostly low-rep model shards) evicted; autoscaler spun up replacements in other racks but some requests hit backoff for ~30s. Seeing a small spike in 503s for a single customer lane (~0.8% of total requests) during the window.

alex: Good context. Can someone ssh to the node?

murtaza: SSH to gpu-node-17 failed (connection reset). I pulled the console logs from cloud provider. Kernel oops / watchdog dump attached below.

murtaza: ```
[  283.912345] NMI watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#2 stuck for 23s!
[  283.915432] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
[  283.916789] Call trace:
[  283.917000]  dump_stack+0x55/0x7b
[  283.917100]  panic+0x101/0x2b4
[  283.917200]  ? gpu_driver_watchdog+0x1a3/0x1f0
[  283.917300]  ? gpu_sched_timeout+0x4f/0x70
```

emily: Noted. This looks like a driver/hardware watchdog rather than kubelet bug, but kubelet NotReady is downstream. Escalating to infra-oncall for hardware check and possible rack investigation.

infra-oncall: I’m up. Oncall here — will reach out to colocation ops. Do we want to cordon the entire rack?

alex: Cordon gpu-node-17 and taint to prevent scheduling while we triage: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` then `kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-17 redwood/maintenance=true:NoSchedule`

murtaza: Done. Node cordoned and tainted.

alex: Start draining non-critical pods to speed recovery: `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

murtaza: Drain in progress. Most model shards moved to other nodes; 2 pods failed to reschedule immediately due to quota, autoscaler is still scaling up.

priya: Customer comms: Emily — recommend informing the affected customers in the 1% impact bucket? Severity appears lower than P1 but still material for those customers.

emily: I’ll open an incident page (internal) and draft a short note for impacted customers. Suggest we mark this as Sev2 for now — will escalate if we see broader degradation.

incident-bot: Incident page created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-gpu-node-17

alex: Any chance we can soft-restart kubelet from the host? If hardware panic happened we need infra to power-cycle.

infra-oncall: Remote power cycle queued with colocation ops. ETA 12 minutes. I’ll watch hardware sensors.

murtaza: I ran a quick kube-apiserver check — eviction events show `kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4389 (tensor-worker) score 153` then GPU driver reported hang. Likely memory leak in model worker combined with driver edge-case.

alex: Can we mitigate by increasing replicas for impacted deployments temporarily to absorb traffic while infra handles hardware?

priya: Autoscaler is already adding nodes but it’s slow. I’ll bump the min replicas for the affected deployment groups by +2 for the next 30 minutes.

priya: Done — pods coming up in other racks. 503s are dropping back toward baseline.

emily: Customer note draft: "We experienced a brief service disruption impacting a small percentage of requests due to a GPU host hardware failure. Traffic failed over to other hosts; recovery actions are underway. No customer data was affected." Will share to #customers-notify after review.

alex: Good. Any logs from the node after power-cycle?

infra-oncall: Colocation ops completed a power cycle at ~1964568200. Node is booting, kernel puked again in early boot logs — looks like persistent hardware fault. We’re scheduling the node for hardware replacement.

murtaza: Given repeated kernel panics we should mark gpu-node-17 as UNRELIABLE and move workloads off permanently. I’ll cordon it indefinitely.

alex: Agreed. Add a placeholder to inventory for RMA.

dina: I’m next oncall in 2 hours. Handoff: track INC-2026, infra replacement ticket INF-4732, pods impacted list pinned to the incident page. Next steps: confirm RMA, ensure autoscaler returns to baseline after replacement, and create a postmortem if we hit any customer-level SLA.

emily: I’ll coordinate the RCA and include a timeline. For now customer impact limited and mitigated.

alex: Thanks all. Closing pager. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Alert acknowledged by alex at 1964567902. Incident escalations: none further.

incident-bot: Handoff complete — transferring watch to @dina for the night shift. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-host-failure (steps followed: cordon, drain, escalate to infra, RMA).

dina: Taking watch. Will check on replacement progress and the incident page.

emily: Adding timeline & summary to the incident page; will ping for postmortem sync tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
